title: Molecules and morals: learning the link (SOP6)

sentences.en: Oxytocin has been called the love hormone, but recent research has shown that the brain chemical may play a role in regulating our moral behaviors, earning itself another nickname,
sentences.zh: 催产素一直被称为“爱情荷尔蒙”，但最近的研究表明，这种大脑化学物质可能在调节我们的道德行为方面发挥作用，因此它又获得了一个绰号，

sentences.en: the moral molecule.
sentences.zh: “道德分子”。

sentences.en: In this episode, psychologist Paul Zak talks about his research into oxytocin's impact on how we interact with one another face-to-face and even virtually.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，心理学家保罗·扎克将探讨他的研究，内容涉及催产素如何影响我们面对面甚至虚拟的互动方式。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·

sentences.en: Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学谈话》。

sentences.en: Paul Zak is the founding director of the Center for Neuroeconomic Studies and professor of economics, psychology, and management at Claremont
sentences.zh: 保罗·扎克是神经经济学研究中心的创始主任，也是克莱蒙特

sentences.en: Graduate University.
sentences.zh: 研究生大学的经济学、心理学和管理学教授。

sentences.en: He studies the brain chemical oxytocin and its impact on behaviors and personality.
sentences.zh: 他研究大脑化学物质催产素及其对行为和个性的影响。

sentences.en: His book, The Moral Molecule, The Source of Love and Prosperity, was published in 2012.
sentences.zh: 他的著作《道德分子：爱与繁荣的源泉》于2012年出版。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Zak.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，扎克博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: We want to know, what is oxytocin?
sentences.zh: 我们想知道，什么是催产素？

sentences.en: Why do you call it the moral molecule?
sentences.zh: 为什么你称它为“道德分子”？

sentences.en: So oxytocin is a chemical the brain makes.
sentences.zh: 催产素是大脑产生的一种化学物质。

sentences.en: It functions both as a hormone, which means it affects parts of the body outside the brain.
sentences.zh: 它既是一种荷尔蒙，这意味着它会影响大脑以外的身体部位。

sentences.en: And in the brain, it actually affects brain activity.
sentences.zh: 同时它在大脑中也会直接影响大脑活动。

sentences.en: And it was known only to be released in humans during birth and breastfeeding and during sex.
sentences.zh: 过去人们只知道它在人类分娩、哺乳和性行为期间会释放。

sentences.en: But it turns out, in studies we started doing about a dozen years ago, that there are many other stimuli that cause the brain to release oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，在大约十二年前我们开始的研究中，发现还有许多其他刺激也会导致大脑释放催产素。

sentences.en: And when oxytocin is released, we connect to other people.
sentences.zh: 当催产素释放时，我们会与他人建立联系。

sentences.en: We care about other people in tangible ways.
sentences.zh: 我们会以切实的方式关心他人。

sentences.en: So we've done experiments where we tempt people with virtual advice by putting money on the table.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一些实验，通过在桌上放钱来诱导人们进行虚拟建议。

sentences.en: And when people release oxytocin or when we give them synthetic oxytocin, they're much more likely to engage in
sentences.zh: 当人们释放催产素，或者我们给他们注射合成催产素时，他们更有可能参与

sentences.en: positive social behaviors, what we would call moral behaviors, because of oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 积极的社会行为，也就是我们所说的道德行为，这正是催产素的作用。

sentences.en: We've taken blood before and after different social stimuli, positive social stimuli, like dancing, like singing, like sharing, people praying, meditating.
sentences.zh: 我们在不同的社会刺激前后采集了血液，这些积极的社会刺激包括跳舞、唱歌、分享、祈祷和冥想。

sentences.en: All these things done in a group release oxytocin and subsequently follow the money.
sentences.zh: 所有这些集体活动都会释放催产素，随后我们观察金钱的流向。

sentences.en: So see what people do with the money once they've released oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 看看人们在释放催产素后会如何处理这些钱。

sentences.en: And we see that we can actually turn on these positive social behaviors, moral behaviors like opening a garden hose.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，我们确实可以像打开花园水管一样，开启这些积极的社会行为，即道德行为。

sentences.en: So what it tells us is that, first of all, oxytocin is a deep part of our human nature.
sentences.zh: 所以这告诉我们，首先，催产素是我们人性深处的一部分。

sentences.en: It's what it means to be a human is to be a social creature.
sentences.zh: 身为人类，意味着我们是社会性生物。

sentences.en: But to be social, we have to have some chemical, some indicator in our brain that tells us this person is safe, this person is someone I can
sentences.zh: 但要进行社交，我们大脑中必须有一种化学物质或指标，告诉我们这个人是安全的，这个人是我可以

sentences.en: affiliate with, this is someone I should care about.
sentences.zh: 结交的，这个人是我应该关心的。

sentences.en: And that's what oxytocin seems to do.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎正是催产素的作用。

sentences.en: So it works in conjunction with other neurochemicals that maintain a balance between trust and distrust or fear, safety, approach, withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 它与其他神经化学物质协同工作，在信任与不信任，或恐惧、安全、接近、退缩之间保持平衡。

sentences.en: Can you alter the level of oxytocin in your brain?
sentences.zh: 你能改变大脑中催产素的水平吗？

sentences.en: Or is that only something you can do in the lab?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只能在实验室里做到？

sentences.en: Or can you do it at home?
sentences.zh: 或者你在家里也能做到？

sentences.en: No, we're doing it all the time.
sentences.zh: 不，我们一直在这样做。

sentences.en: So a simple thing like hugging will raise oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 比如拥抱这样简单的事情就能提高催产素水平。

sentences.en: So a number of years ago, I decided to not shake people's hands, but hug everybody.
sentences.zh: 多年前，我决定不再与人握手，而是拥抱每一个人。

sentences.en: And people would connect better with me, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们确实会与我建立更好的联系。

sentences.en: And so surprisingly, yeah, surprisingly.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，是的，确实令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And so anything that really reaches out and connects you to other people will likely raise oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 所以任何真正伸出援手并让你与他人建立联系的行为，都可能会提高催产素水平。

sentences.en: We've done a lot of field studies, for example, in the jungles of
sentences.zh: 我们做过很多实地研究，例如在巴布亚新几内亚的丛林中，

sentences.en: Papua New Guinea, taking blood from people who live in the rainforest after they do a tribal dance.
sentences.zh: 采集那些生活在雨林中的人在跳完部落舞蹈后的血液。

sentences.en: And the majority of those individuals release oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数人都会释放催产素。

sentences.en: I've gone to weddings and taken blood from the bride and the groom and the wedding party.
sentences.zh: 我参加过婚礼，并采集了新娘、新郎和婚礼参与者的血液。

sentences.en: And that wedding ritual not only releases oxytocin on average, but it does so in a very particular manner.
sentences.zh: 那种婚礼仪式不仅平均能释放催产素，而且是以一种非常独特的方式进行的。

sentences.en: You know, who's the center of the wedding solar system?
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁是婚礼太阳系的中心吗？

sentences.en: The bride, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然是新娘。

sentences.en: She has the biggest really increase in oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 她的催产素水平增加得最多。

sentences.en: Who loves the wedding almost as much as the bride?
sentences.zh: 谁像新娘一样爱这场婚礼？

sentences.en: Her mother, right?
sentences.zh: 她的母亲，对吧？

sentences.en: So she's number two.
sentences.zh: 所以她是第二名。

sentences.en: And so the release of oxytocin, the amount of release, tells us about the strength of connections between individuals.
sentences.zh: 因此，催产素的释放量告诉我们个体之间联系的强度。

sentences.en: So who are the best oxytocin releasers?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁是最好的催产素释放者呢？

sentences.en: Little children?
sentences.zh: 小孩子吗？

sentences.en: Puppies?
sentences.zh: 小狗吗？

sentences.en: You know, people who need our support to survive.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些需要我们支持才能生存的人。

sentences.en: But I think we all can actually release oxytocin in others.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们所有人其实都能激发他人体内的催产素。

sentences.en: So we can't cause our own brains to release oxytocin in general.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们通常无法让自己大脑分泌催产素。

sentences.en: There's some exceptions, but we can give that gift to others.
sentences.zh: 虽然有一些例外，但我们可以把这份礼物送给别人。

sentences.en: So I think one of the take-homes is, as a social creature, you need to reach out, connect to others, give them that gift of oxytocin release.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为其中一个要点是，作为一种社会性生物，你需要走出去，与他人建立联系，给予他们催产素分泌的礼物。

sentences.en: And most likely, 95% of the thousands of people we study, they will reciprocate.
sentences.zh: 而且很有可能，在我们研究的成千上万的人中，95%的人会做出回应。

sentences.en: So the people who don't are essentially of two types.
sentences.zh: 所以那些没有回应的人基本上分为两类。

sentences.en: One is people who are super stressed out.
sentences.zh: 一类是压力极大的人。

sentences.en: They're having a bad day.
sentences.zh: 他们正经历糟糕的一天。

sentences.en: They just don't have the brain activity to actually release oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 他们的大脑活动不足以真正分泌催产素。

sentences.en: And the second is psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 第二类是精神病患者。

sentences.en: So our study of psychopaths shows that they don't release oxytocin, and they don't have the antecedent
sentences.zh: 我们对精神病患者的研究表明，他们不会分泌催产素，也没有催产素分泌的前因，

sentences.en: psychological effects of oxytocin release, which is that feeling of empathy.
sentences.zh: 也就是那种同理心的感觉。

sentences.en: So that's classically missing in psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 所以这在精神病患者身上是典型缺失的。

sentences.en: So when we connect to others, we better reflect their emotions, which helps us be better social creatures to understand how to interact with them.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们与他人建立联系时，我们能更好地反映他们的情绪，这有助于我们成为更好的社会性生物，去理解如何与他们互动。

sentences.en: And you're talking about things that are very much about face-to-face interactions.
sentences.zh: 你谈论的这些事情非常强调面对面的互动。

sentences.en: How have our brains adapted to more frequent interactions via social media and online networking?
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑是如何适应通过社交媒体和在线网络进行的更频繁的互动的？

sentences.en: How is all this coming into play?
sentences.zh: 这一切是如何发挥作用的？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So we've done a couple of small-scale studies.
sentences.zh: 我们做过几项小规模的研究。

sentences.en: We came in, had people give us a sample of their blood, and then let them in private use social media of any type.
sentences.zh: 我们让人们提供血液样本，然后让他们在私下里使用任何类型的社交媒体。

sentences.en: Twitter,
sentences.zh: 推特，

sentences.en: Facebook, emailing, and then took their blood 10 minutes later.
sentences.zh: 脸书，发邮件，然后在10分钟后抽取他们的血液。

sentences.en: What we found was that in 100% of the people we've tested so far, social media use causes the brain to release oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，到目前为止我们测试的100%的人中，社交媒体的使用都会导致大脑分泌催产素。

sentences.en: And as I said earlier, the amount of oxytocin release tells us about the strength of connection.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，催产素分泌的量告诉我们联系的强度。

sentences.en: So we did this recently for a Korean TV station, and we included one of their young producers in the sample.
sentences.zh: 我们最近为一家韩国电视台做了这项研究，我们将他们的一位年轻制片人也纳入了样本中。

sentences.en: He must have been 22 or 23 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时一定只有22或23岁。

sentences.en: And when we got his results from his blood test back, he had 150% increase in oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 当我们拿到他的血液检测结果时，他的催产素水平增加了150%。

sentences.en: So I said, I don't know what this guy was doing because he was using social media in private, but my guess was he was interacting with his mother or
sentences.zh: 所以我说，我不知道这家伙在做什么，因为他是在私下使用社交媒体，但我的猜测是他当时正在与他的母亲或

sentences.en: his girlfriend because the connection was so powerful.
sentences.zh: 他的女朋友互动，因为这种联系太强烈了。

sentences.en: They checked.
sentences.zh: 他们核实了一下。

sentences.en: He was posting to his girlfriend's Facebook page for 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在给女朋友的脸书页面发消息，持续了10分钟。

sentences.en: So again, think about this chemical as giving us the ability to determine who we should invest our resources in, who we should be vulnerable to,
sentences.zh: 所以再次思考一下，这种化学物质赋予了我们一种能力，去决定我们应该在谁身上投入资源，我们应该对谁敞开心扉，

sentences.en: who we should trust, who we want to be around.
sentences.zh: 我们应该信任谁，我们想和谁在一起。

sentences.en: And that's very adaptive for social creatures.
sentences.zh: 这对社会性生物来说是非常具有适应性的。

sentences.en: Now, another thing you founded the Center for Neuroeconomic Studies.
sentences.zh: 另外，你创立了神经经济学研究中心。

sentences.en: And what is neuroeconomics?
sentences.zh: 什么是神经经济学？

sentences.en: How does it help us learn about human behavior?
sentences.zh: 它如何帮助我们了解人类行为？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I know that you have never made a bad decision in your life, but your brother-in-law who
sentences.zh: 我知道你这辈子从未做过错误的决定，但你的姐夫/妹夫

sentences.en: started buying investment real estate in 2007, when everyone knew the bubble was going to crash, what's the deal on that?
sentences.zh: 在2007年开始购买投资性房地产，当时每个人都知道泡沫即将破裂，这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So neuroeconomic studies were in activity while people make decisions.
sentences.zh: 神经经济学研究的是人们做决定时的活动。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Many of those decisions have to do with decisions that may involve products or markets, but a lot of them don't.
sentences.zh: 这些决定中很多与涉及产品或市场的决策有关，但也有很多不是。

sentences.en: So much of our research has been on social decisions, so interact strongly with areas in social psychology, as well as with solving probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们的大部分研究都集中在社会决策上，因此与社会心理学领域以及解决问题有着紧密的互动。

sentences.en: How do people actually solve problems as a group or as individuals, which interacts with cognitive psychology?
sentences.zh: 人们实际上是如何以群体或个人的身份解决问题的，这与认知心理学有关。

sentences.en: So many of the studies we've done have a very strong psychological component to them because we not only want to understand the brain activity and the behavior,
sentences.zh: 我们所做的许多研究都有很强的心理学成分，因为我们不仅想了解大脑活动和行为，

sentences.en: but what it feels like.
sentences.zh: 还想了解它的感受。

sentences.en: What's the subjective experience of going through this?
sentences.zh: 经历这一切的主观体验是什么？

sentences.en: And so we use a lot of tools from psychology to really understand what human beings are doing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们使用了很多心理学工具来真正理解人类在做什么。

sentences.en: Well, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Dr. Zak, for being with us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢Zak博士今天能来到这里。

sentences.en: It was a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: For more information on Dr. Zak's work, please visit our website at speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多关于Zak博士工作的信息，请访问我们的网站speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology, I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的《心理学谈话》，我是Audrey Hamilton。
